archetype.name: Retooling (trenches broke down)
archetype.definition: A recent contender, 14-3 two years ago and 11-6 last season, whose lines on both sides have given out, leaving a team whose 2-5 record is an honest reflection of how it plays.

report.headline: The trenches failed on both sides, and the Eagles' record tells the truth.
report.take:
This is not a good team having bad luck. Philadelphia went 14-3 in 2024 and 11-6 last year with a net EPA that ranked 8th. In 2026 the Eagles are 2-5 with a net EPA of -0.173, 30th in the league. Wins over expected (-1.06) says they might be one win light, and their point differential implies 3.1 wins. That is a rounding error, not a hidden playoff team. The Book has seen it too: they have covered in one of six graded games, 31st in cover rate.

The offense breaks down at the line of scrimmage. The run game is stuffed on 30.2% of carries, the worst rate in football. Backs average 2.01 yards before contact (27th) and 3.14 a carry (29th). In back-to-back games against Jacksonville and Carolina the Eagles ran for 22 and 35 yards. Pass protection allows pressure at the 29th-ranked rate. Hurts takes the third-longest time to throw in the league, so the line is not holding up and receivers are not getting open fast enough. The roster around it is thinning. Lane Johnson is out for the season, starting center Jake Majors was a coach's-decision inactive, Barkley has 43 carries in five games and was hurt again Monday, and DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks both sat against Dallas. The result is an offense 30th in EPA and 31st in time of possession.

The defense looks steadier in the box score than it is. Points allowed ranked a middling 17th in the season table, held up by respectable third-down (13th) and red-zone (12th) work and by special teams that rank 6th in EPA and keep flipping the field. Underneath that is a defense with no pass rush. Its QB-hit rate and sack rate are both dead last, it has 8 sacks and 3 takeaways (30th), and it ranks 31st in rush EPA allowed. Dallas ran for 204 yards on it last week. A defense that cannot get home or take the ball away is relying on opponents to stall, and that does not last, least of all one that spends as much time on the field as this one does.

The only reason the season isn't over is the NFC East. The Giants lead at 4-2-1, Dallas is 3-4, and Washington is 1-4-1. The remaining schedule also includes three 2-5 teams in Arizona, Indiana and Houston. The 2020 season (4 wins, net EPA 25th) is the closest precedent in this history, and nothing in the current profile says this team is better than that one. Getting back to respectability depends on getting bodies back on the offensive line and at receiver. A real playoff run would take a turnaround the underlying numbers don't support.

strengths.title: Special teams winning field position
strengths.body: The Eagles rank 6th in special-teams EPA per game. That is the one phase consistently adding value, and it gives a stalled offense shorter fields and a tired defense longer ones. Kicking and coverage hold up better than offense or defense from game to game, so this should last, but it adds a few points a game, not wins on its own.

strengths.title: Holding up in high-leverage downs
strengths.body: Despite allowing yards at a 26th-ranked clip, the defense is 13th on third down and 12th in red-zone touchdown rate. That is why points allowed have stayed mid-pack rather than collapsing. With no pass rush and a leaky run defense, this kind of bend-don't-break resistance tends to fade, and the 38 points Dallas scored may be the first sign of it.

strengths.title: Coverage depth past the top receiver
strengths.body: Second and third receivers have been held well under their usual output, both 6th in the league in PPR points over average, and WR3s are producing negative EPA per target. The corners behind the top cover man are doing their jobs. The cost is that opponents' WR1s feast (29th), and with Michael Carter II and Jakorian Bennett out, the depth that makes this work is thinner now.

concerns.title: An offensive line that can't block
concerns.body: A league-worst stuff rate and 29th-ranked pressure rate allowed mean the Eagles can neither stay on schedule on the ground nor give Hurts a clean pocket. Hurts holding the ball 3.036 seconds makes the pressure worse, a sign that receivers aren't winning early either. With Lane Johnson out for the season and the center position in flux, this is a personnel problem, not a slump, and it won't fix itself.

concerns.title: No pass rush, no takeaways
concerns.body: The defense is last in the league in both QB-hit rate and sack rate, has 8 sacks and has forced 3 turnovers. Quarterbacks are rarely disrupted, so drives rarely end early, and opponents' top receivers get open (WR1s are 28th in EPA per target). Takeaways swing year to year, but a missing pass rush is structural, and Nolan Smith Jr.'s concussion takes away one of the few edge players who play regularly.

concerns.title: Run defense getting pushed around
concerns.body: The defense is 31st in rush EPA allowed, and Dallas just ran for 204 yards. Paired with an offense that can't sustain drives, this keeps the defense on the field and lets opponents milk clocks with leads. Unless the front adds bodies, it is likely to keep happening.

trend.note: The Eagles opened with narrow wins over Washington and Tennessee, failing to cover as favorites both times, and have lost every game since. The two most recent losses were the worst, a home loss to Carolina with Tanner McKee at quarterback and a 38-21 beating by Dallas with Hurts back.

nextGame.headline: Underdogs to a 1-4-1 rival, and the Book has reasons
nextGame.body:
This is a meeting of two bottom-ten teams by net EPA. Washington's defense is exploitable: it allows touchdowns on 81.8% of red-zone trips, the worst rate in the league, ranks 27th in pass EPA allowed, and offenses throw against it more than against anyone. It does take away big runs, allowing the 2nd-lowest explosive run rate, which pushes this game onto Hurts' arm. Washington's offense is middling (18th) but protects the ball, and its +1 turnover margin per game ranks 3rd. Its pressure rate (9th) lines up against an Eagles line that has been overwhelmed. The Eagles won the Week 1 meeting 24-22 at home behind 136 rushing yards and no turnovers. The Book still makes Washington a 4.5-point favorite with a 40.5 total, and Philadelphia is +170.

Availability favors Washington. Smith and Wicks sat last week with return estimates pointing at this game, Barkley is questionable after a hamstring led to a back problem, Johnson is gone for the year, and Majors was benched. Nolan Smith Jr. (concussion) and Michael Carter II (abdomen) are also listed out. Washington has lost Terry McLaurin for the season and Jaylin Lane to IR, which thins its receiving corps. Defensive linemen Javon Kinlaw and Charles Omenihu are questionable, and their status matters most against this Eagles line. Jayden Daniels has started the last two games, with Marcus Mariota questionable behind him.

waysToWin.title: Feed Goedert against Washington's tight-end leak
waysToWin.body: Washington has been the worst defense in the league against tight ends, both in PPR points over average and near the bottom in EPA per target. With the receiver room banged up, Goedert is the most reliable mismatch Hurts has. Quick throws to him also take some heat off a struggling pass protection.

waysToWin.title: Finish drives with fourth-down aggression
waysToWin.body: Washington turns red-zone trips into touchdowns at the league's worst rate, and the Eagles have gone for it on every fourth down they were credited with, the most aggressive rate in the league. An offense this inefficient can't settle for field goals. Being aggressive inside the 30 against this defense is where the Eagles' points have to come from.

waysToWin.title: Win the hidden yardage
waysToWin.body: Philadelphia's special teams rank 6th in EPA per game, and Washington's rank 26th. In a game the Book expects to be low-scoring and close, a big return or a pinned punt can decide it. It is the clearest edge the Eagles hold in any phase.

waysToLose.title: Washington's rush overwhelms the patched line
waysToLose.body: Washington generates pressure at the 9th-best rate, and the Eagles allow it at the 29th-worst, now without Johnson. Hurts holding the ball over three seconds makes it worse. If Kinlaw and Omenihu play, drives could die on second-and-long before Goedert ever gets involved.

waysToLose.title: Washington runs it down their throat
waysToLose.body: Washington's line creates 3.21 yards before contact, 3rd in the league. The Eagles are 31st in rush EPA allowed, and Dallas just ran for 204 yards on them. If Washington can lean on the run, it controls the clock and keeps a struggling Eagles offense on the sideline.

waysToLose.title: Losing the turnover battle again
waysToLose.body: Washington is +1 per game in turnover margin, 3rd in the league, while the Eagles have 3 takeaways all season. One giveaway, like the three in the Chicago loss, probably decides a game with a 40.5 total. The Eagles have shown no way to get that possession back.

nextGame.watch: Whether the reshuffled offensive line can give Hurts a clean first two reads against Washington's pass rush. If it can't, nothing else in the game plan matters.

restOfSeason.body:
The schedule offers chances: two games against the Giants, a trip to Dallas, and Arizona, Indiana and Houston, all 2-5. The NFC East is weak enough that a winning stretch would make the standings interesting again. Pittsburgh, Seattle and a trip to San Francisco look like losses for a team playing like this. The special-teams edge and the solid third-down defense are the parts most likely to hold. The red-zone resistance is the part most likely to slip, because a defense with no pass rush and a soft run front eventually gives up touchdowns, not just yards.

The upside depends on health more than scheme. Getting Smith, Wicks and a healthy Barkley back, and settling the interior line, would lift an offense that has been playing with a patchwork roster. Even then, the offensive line's stuff and pressure rates point to a team that wins some winnable games and loses most of the rest. Expect something around 5 or 6 wins, with the division the only realistic, and unlikely, way into January.
swingFactors: Offensive line health and the center job
Return of Smith, Wicks and Barkley
Whether the defense finds any pass rush or takeaways

confidence.note: Seven games and the efficiency and talent signals agree, but the injury list is long and in flux.
